city_center.name: Downtown St. Louis / Gateway Arch riverfront
city_center.landmark: The Gateway Arch above the Mississippi River; red-brick neighborhoods (Soulard, The Hill) that define the city's built texture
city_center.notes: St. Louis sits on the Mississippi River as the historic gateway west; the city is famous for its red-brick housing stock and neighborhoods, and for St. Louis-style barbecue -- spare ribs associated with the region. Schnucks (founded north St. Louis 1939) and Dierbergs split the local grocery market. sources: St. Louis-style barbecue (en.wikipedia.org); Schnucks history (schnucks.com/about); Dierbergs splits STL market (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dierbergs_Markets).

cultural_notes: St. Louis is defined by its red-brick building stock -- rowhouses and neighborhood churches in areas like Soulard and The Hill -- a foundational regional building material and visual texture (INFERRED architectural framing from region knowledge -- verify specific claims before production)

St. Louis-style barbecue refers to spare ribs associated with the St. Louis area -- a defining regional food identity distinct from Kansas City-style (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis-style_barbecue)

Schnucks was founded in north St. Louis in 1939 and Dierbergs is based in Chesterfield; the two family-owned chains effectively split the Greater St. Louis grocery market among local retailers -- strong local-grocer loyalty (source: schnucks.com/about; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dierbergs_Markets)

St. Louis has one of the largest Bosnian diaspora communities in the US, concentrated in the Bevo Mill / south-city area -- creative should acknowledge a multi-heritage neighborhood identity (INFERRED framing -- verify before production use)
